module_title: Basics of Light, Reflection, and Refraction
introduction: Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation that enables us to see. It travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation) and has a dual nature (behaves as both a wave and a particle/photon).

core_concepts.title: Speed of Light
core_concepts.description: Light travels fastest in a vacuum. Its speed is $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$. It travels slightly slower in air, much slower in water, and even slower in glass.

core_concepts.title: Reflection of Light
core_concepts.description:
The bouncing back of light rays into the same medium after hitting a smooth surface. 
Laws of Reflection: 
1. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection ($i = r$). 
2. The incident ray, reflected ray, and normal all lie in the same plane.

core_concepts.title: Real vs. Virtual Images
core_concepts.description:
1. Real Image: Formed when light rays 'actually' intersect. It can be captured on a screen and is always 'Inverted' (upside down). 
2. Virtual Image: Formed when light rays 'appear' to meet when produced backward. It cannot be captured on a screen and is always 'Erect' (straight up).

core_concepts.title: Refraction of Light
core_concepts.description:
The bending of light when it passes from one transparent medium to another (e.g., from air to water). This happens because light changes its speed in different mediums. 
Example: A pencil dipped in water appears bent or broken.

important_entities.name: Plane Mirror
important_entities.significance: The image formed by a plane mirror is always Virtual, Erect, and of the SAME size as the object. However, it suffers from 'Lateral Inversion' (the left side of the object appears as the right side of the image, which is why 'AMBULANCE' is written backward on vehicles).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Objects that emit their own light are 'Luminous' (Sun, bulb). Objects that don't are 'Non-luminous' (Earth, wood). The Moon is NON-LUMINOUS; it merely reflects the Sun's light.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: RDA: Rarer to Denser = Approaches normal. DRA: Denser to Rarer = Away from normal.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: When light goes from Air (Rarer) to Water (Denser), it bends 'towards' the normal line.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent SSC question: 'Why does a lemon kept in a glass of water appear larger?' Answer: Due to Refraction of light.
